references.text: Parallel text describing the same law regarding faithlessness to the Lord and lying to one's neighbor about entrusted property.
Prohibition against lying, deceiving each other, stealing, and oppressing one's neighbor - the same themes mentioned in the verse.
Concerns faithlessness (ma'al) toward the Lord and guilt toward fellow humans, with a requirement for confession and restitution.
Prohibition against oppressing (ashaq) a poor and needy worker; the same word is used for oppression.
The prophet mentions theft, robbery, and oppression as sins the people commit against one another.
Concerns deception and oppression through false weights and dishonest trade.
Warns against relying on robbery and oppression (gazal and ashaq).
Refers to extortion and bribery, similar sins against fellow humans.
Earlier verses in the same chapter that define ma'al (faithlessness) toward the Lord and its consequences.
Jesus teaches that one must be reconciled with one's brother before bringing an offering, related to guilt toward fellow humans.
